questions.q: Social cognition is the cognitive processes that influence ____.
questions.explanation: Social cognition refers to the cognitive processes (perceiving, interpreting, remembering information about others) that influence social behavior.

questions.q: Smooth and adaptive social interactions depend on the recruitment of ____.
questions.explanation: Smooth and adaptive social interaction draws on several cognitive processes at once, including perception, attention and language, so all the options apply.

questions.q: Which of the following abilities does not come under social cognition?
questions.explanation: Face processing, joint attention and moral reasoning are social-cognitive abilities. Rote memory is a general memory function, not specifically social cognition.

questions.q: Social cognition develops primarily in old age.
questions.explanation: False. Social cognition develops from infancy through childhood and adolescence into adulthood; it does not primarily develop in old age.

questions.q: A theory of mind refers to a person’s ability to understand and think about the ____ of other people.
questions.explanation: Theory of mind is the ability to attribute mental states (beliefs, desires, intentions, knowledge) to others and to understand that these may differ from one's own.

questions.q: The ____ theory details the processes of observational learning and modeling, and the influence of self-efficacy on the production of behavior.
questions.explanation: Bandura's social-cognitive theory explains learning through observation and modeling, and stresses self-efficacy as a key influence on whether behavior is produced.

questions.q: ____ processes account for the information that is selected for observation in the environment.
questions.explanation: In Bandura's model, attentional processes determine what is selected for observation in the environment. Retention, production and motivational processes come after attention.

questions.q: Children become more aggressive when they observe aggressive or violent models.
questions.explanation: True. Bandura's Bobo doll studies showed that children who observed aggressive models were more likely to imitate aggressive behavior.

questions.q: The ____ model of observational learning involves real or fictional characters displaying behaviors in books, films, television programs, or online media.
questions.explanation: A symbolic model is a real or fictional character shown in books, films, television or online media. A live model is a person physically present, and a verbal instructional model describes the behavior in words.

questions.q: ____ refers to the anticipated consequences of a person’s behavior.
questions.explanation: Outcome expectations are the anticipated consequences of a person's behavior. Self-efficacy, by contrast, is the belief in one's ability to perform the behavior.
